products.name: PCD (Portable Context Deck)
products.note: Portable context layer served over MCP; preferences, traits, skills, work state and knowledge in one deck loaded into any MCP-capable client; AGPL-3.0 public core; early access

reading.body:
Portablecontext.ai offers a standardized layer to port user context across AI clients, addressing fragmentation in how different systems store and access personal information.

The product consolidates preferences, traits, skills, work state, and knowledge into a single portable deck served over MCP protocol. This targets a real friction point: as AI tools proliferate, users duplicate their context setup across incompatible platforms. A standardized, portable format reduces that duplication and lets users switch between clients without losing their configuration state.

For AI infrastructure, this matters because context management sits between the user and the model. If context is locked into proprietary systems, it creates switching costs that fragment the market. If it is portable, users can more easily adopt new tools as compute becomes cheaper or capability improvements justify migration. An open protocol for context also reduces the computational overhead of context replication, though this data does not specify whether portability itself saves cycles.

The company is early stage with a single product in early access and no tracked funding, litigation, or regulatory filings. The data does not cover whether the MCP ecosystem has adopted this format, how many clients support it, or whether users actually switch between systems at a rate that makes portability valuable in practice.

profile_text.body:
portablecontext.ai is a Belgium-based company whose site describes PCD, the Portable Context Deck, as a portable context layer that can be loaded into any AI. The site says PCD uses open formats and can export to JSON and Markdown. Andrea Dellanoce is listed as operator and data controller.

The company's tracked product is PCD (Portable Context Deck), placed in the notes, knowledge and meetings category. It is described as a portable context layer served over MCP, holding preferences, traits, skills, work state and knowledge in one deck that loads into any MCP-capable client. The public core is under AGPL-3.0, and the product is at an early access stage.

The held record lists no lawsuits and no MCP servers for the company.
